examples.text: 彼の英語は本当にすごい。
現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Read にほん (Nihon) or にっぽん (Nippon).

examples.text: 日本の文化が好きです。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: こないだ正式に退学しました。
examples.trans: I officially withdrew from university the other day.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

examples.text: こないだ正式に退学しました。
examples.trans: I officially withdrew from university the other day.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Casual/intimate apology, often softened with な or ね.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

examples.text: 盛り上がってるとこごめんね。取材が入ってるから。
examples.trans: Sorry to interrupt the moment, she has a press interview scheduled.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Godan verb: potential polite 入れます (はいれます) means 'can enter'.

examples.text: 予約なしでも入れますか。
examples.trans: Can we get in without a reservation?

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Godan intransitive verb.

examples.text: 仕事に戻って稼いでくれ。
examples.trans: Go back to work and earn money.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).

examples.text: いない間持ちこたえてくれて、ありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you for holding everything together while I was gone.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.note: 頑張ります! is the classic cheerful commitment when starting a job or task.

examples.trans: I will do my best today too.
Do your best on the exam!

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Very common colloquial pronunciation/variant of すみません.

examples.text: すいません、ちょっと通してください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, please let me through.

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: from now on; in the future; now
meanings.note: Time expression referring to the immediate or upcoming future.

examples.text: これから家へ帰ります。

examples.trans: The real test starts from here.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
